claim_1.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from first-cohort volunteers (n = 6 subjects/group; 162 samples in total) across the study time points, using linear mixed models with contrasts versus baseline, false discovery rate adjustment, and a fold-change >2 cutoff, showed that a robust set of 239 transcripts was significantly altered in response to vaccination compared to the average of the two baseline time points.

sources.quote: Specific time points where significant differences were found in comparison to baseline for each group (false discovery rate [FDR] = 0.10) were identified. Of the 3,102 transcripts for which abundance was significantly altered in response to vaccines, 239 changed by more than 2-fold in at least one time point.

Figure 1 Blood Transcriptional Profiles of Vaccinated Subjects(A) Patterns of changes in transcript abundance are shown on a heatmap for a robust set of 239 transcripts using an FDR of 0.10 and fold change >2). For each subject, data are normalized to the average of the two baseline time points.

claim_47.claim: microarray analysis of whole blood from healthy adults aged 18 to 64 years receiving seasonal influenza vaccine or pneumococcal vaccine, using modular fingerprint correlation analysis with Spearman correlations on day 7 baseline-normalized averaged modular expression profiles, showed that day 7 module M3.3 expression was positively associated with day 28/baseline fold change of antibody titer for all available pneumococcal serotypes in the pneumococcal vaccine group.

sources.quote: The strongest positive correlations were found for modules M3.3 (annotated as cell cycle) and M4.11 (plasma cells) and to a lesser extent M4.10 (B cells), M5.10 and M6.2 (both associated with mitochondrial respiration).

Correlations between day 7 baseline-normalized averaged modular expression profiles and fold change of day 28 antibody titer over baseline for all available pneumococcal serotypes and influenza vaccine strains are represented on a heatmap. Modules are shown in rows and serotypes in columns. Red indicates strong positive correlation, and blue indicates strong negative correlation. (A) shows pneumococcal vaccine, and (B) shows influenza vaccine (D28/baseline fold change [FC] in virus neutralization [VN] and hemagglutinin [HAI] titers). An interactive supplement is available for this figure that allows users to dynamically filter modules and select additional parameters for correlation (iFigure 7: http://www.interactivefigures.com/dm3/vaccine-paper/figure-7.gsp). Correlations and associated p values were calculated via the Spearman method and can be adjusted by using a slider; Benjamini-Hochberg multiple testing correction is controlled by an on/off toggle.
